app.title: пташечка — cross stitch & bead pattern designer
app.description: Turn a paper cross stitch chart into a digital one — Autofill reads the symbols off a photo, block by block. Key, chart, totals, PDF, Pattern Keeper and OXS files.
app.dragToMove: Drag to move · double-click to put back
app.resizePanel: Drag to resize · double-click for the default width

tools.eraser: Eraser (E) — erases crosses, beads, partial stitches, knots and backstitch. Point at a backstitch line to delete only that line

tools.select: Select (S) — drag a box; Shift adds
tools.magicWand: Magic wand (W) — same key, connected; Shift+click selects all of that key
tools.partial: Partial stitches (Q cycles quarter / three-quarter / petite)
tools.override: Override (O): when on, drawing replaces stitches already on the chart. Off = only empty squares are filled.
tools.autofill: Autofill (Shift+F) — reads a 10 × 10 block off the image behind the chart
tools.pausedForImage: The tools wait while you edit the image behind the chart (U or Esc to finish)

straighten.title: Straighten the chart photo
straighten.hint: Drag the 4 corners onto corners of the chart’s grid on the photo — the outer border works best. The blue lines show where the grid will fall; arrow keys nudge the last corner by 1 px (Shift: 10).
straighten.crossed: Corners are crossed — put them in order: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left

points.1: The quickest way from a paper chart to a digital one.
points.2: 9 short steps — a couple of minutes.
points.3: Come back any time: <hl>☰ ▸ Quick start guide</hl>.

points.1: Open <hl>Pattern ▸ New ▸ Blank pattern</hl>.
points.2: Enter the size in stitches — as on the paper chart.

key.title: 2. The key

points.1: Every line of the paper key: <hl>+ Add to key</hl>.

key.tip: Keep the key in view: <hl>References ▸ Add a photo window</hl> (the picture icon at the bottom of the side panel). Tick off added lines with its <hl>marker</hl>.

trace.title: 3. Chart behind the stitches

points.1: Add the chart photo: <hl>References ▸ Image behind the chart</hl> — the picture icon at the bottom of the side panel.
points.2: Drag the <hl>4 corners</hl> onto the grid corners — the photo lies flat.
points.3: Trace the symbols with the key entries.

trace.tip: Photo not perfect? Zoom in and press the <hl>edit image</hl> button by the zoom (or U): a <hl>frame</hl> appears — drag its side and the photo under it follows, the photo’s opposite side stays in place.

autofill.title: 4. Autofill — the fast way

points.1: Stitch a few cells of each symbol by hand.
points.2: Pick <hl>Autofill</hl> (Shift+F) and click the 10 × 10 block you’ve lined up.
points.3: It shows what it found — <hl>Accept</hl> or <hl>Decline</hl>, then on to the next block.
points.4: Works best when every key symbol looks exactly like the paper chart’s — draw your own where needed.

autofill.tip: It only fills cells it’s sure about. Check the result — it gets better the more you mark.

points.1: <hl>Colour</hl> — check the colours.
<hl>Ctrl/⌘ + Z</hl> — undo.
points.2: Hold <hl>Alt/⌥</hl> — pick a colour from the chart.
points.4: By default drawing never overwrites filled squares. Need to? Turn on <hl>Override</hl> (O).

points.1: Your work saves itself — in this browser, and in your account when you’re signed in.
points.2: Not signed in? Browsers can wipe what they keep — now and then use <hl>Download work file (.xbird)</hl>.

points.1: Made a mess? <hl>Versions</hl> (🕘 at the bottom of the side panel) bring back an earlier state.
In <hl>Pattern info</hl> (ⓘ at the bottom of the side panel) fill in the <hl>name</hl> and <hl>author</hl> — Хрестики show them.
points.2: Finished? The <hl>printer button</hl>: a <hl>PDF chart to print</hl>, Pattern Keeper, images — and an <hl>Open Cross Stitch file (.oxs)</hl> for Хрестики and Ruta Stitch.

points.1: Your e-copy is ready.
points.2: The guide is always here: <hl>☰ ▸ Quick start guide</hl>.

points.1: The <hl>edit</hl> button by the zoom turns it on and off (or U).
points.2: Zoom in and a <hl>frame</hl> appears in the middle: drag its side and the photo under it follows the cursor.
points.3: <hl>↺ ↻</hl> above the frame turn the photo a little, <hl>Ctrl/⌘+Z</hl> undoes.

referenceTip.title: A photo in its own window

points.1: Put the paper chart’s <hl>key</hl> here to keep it in view.
points.2: Or the <hl>chart scan</hl> — if you’d rather not put it behind the stitches.
points.3: Drag the window, resize it, change its opacity.

points.1: <hl>Marker</hl> — paint over what you’ve already copied: key lines or parts of the chart.
points.2: <hl>Shade stitched</hl> — the window shades the squares that are already on the chart (when the photo is the whole chart).

autofillPrepare.title: Autofill: before you start

points.1: Make the <hl>key</hl> first — Autofill fills cells with its entries.
points.2: Put the chart under the stitches: <hl>Image behind the chart</hl>.
points.3: <hl>Stitch a few cells of each symbol by hand.</hl> Autofill only sees the symbols it has already learned from your stitches.

autofillPrepare.tip: Make every key symbol look exactly like the paper chart’s — draw your own where there’s no match. Autofill works best that way.

points.1: Before you click, make sure the <hl>10 × 10 block</hl> you want to fill sits exactly on the photo.
points.2: Not quite? Turn on <hl>image editing</hl> (U), nudge the photo, then turn it off again.

points.1: Autofill fills only the cells it’s sure about and leaves the rest empty.
points.2: It can still make a mistake — glance over every block before you accept it.
points.3: The more you stitch by hand, the better it gets.

points.1: The faint symbols in the block are its suggestions — nothing is on the chart yet.
points.2: <hl>Accept</hl> (Enter) puts them on the chart, <hl>Decline</hl> (Esc) drops them. Either way, click the next block.
points.3: Point at <hl>Decline</hl> for advice when the result isn’t right.

points.1: <hl>Symbols only</hl> — show the suggestions as symbols, or on their colour. Just this preview.
points.2: <hl>Hold the eye</hl> — the suggestions disappear while you hold it, so you can compare with the photo.

points.1: Each key entry gets a symbol — pick one from the row or from <hl>All…</hl>.
points.2: Nothing like the paper chart’s? <hl>Draw your own</hl> with the pencil: circles, squares, stars, lines, arrows — filled, outlined or cut out.
points.3: Most useful with <hl>Autofill</hl>: it works best when every symbol looks exactly like the one on the paper chart.
